source: Day, Night and the Sun's Path
The Earth spins once about every 24 hours. The side facing the Sun has day; the other side has night. The Sun seems to rise in the east and set in the west because the Earth turns.
Thinking the Sun moves around the Earth each day, or that the Sun goes behind the Moon at night. The Earth's spin makes day and night.
Every morning the Sun appears in the east, crosses the sky and sets in the west. It looks as if the Sun moves around us. It is really the Earth that turns.

The Earth spins (rotates) on its axis once about every 24 hours. The half facing the Sun has day; the half facing away has night. Because Earth spins toward the east, the Sun seems to rise in the east and set in the west.
Turn the Earth. The dot is you: is it day or night where you are?
Shadows change during the day too. In the morning and evening, when the Sun is low, shadows are long. Near noon, when the Sun is high, they are short. A shadow always points away from the Sun.
A stick's shadow during the day.

Thinking the Sun goes around the Earth, or that night comes when the Moon covers the Sun. Night is our side of Earth turned away from the Sun.
